title: Shafarevich Feasibility: Abelian Case Proved, Full Theorem Needs Embedding Problems
description: Answers the open question: Can Shafarevich's theorem (every finite solvable group is realizable as a Galois group over ℚ) be proved in Lean using Mathlib's developing class field theory? Answer: YES for cyclic groups (proved via Dirichlet + Galois fixed fields in InverseGalois.lean) and coprime products (proved here via CRT: ℤ/mℤ × ℤ/nℤ ≅ ℤ/(mn)ℤ when gcd(m,n)=1). For general abelian groups, one gap remains: linear disjointness of cyclotomic subfields at different primes (~500 lines). Full Shafarevich needs embedding problem theory (Brauer groups, Galois cohomology, Tate-Poitou duality) — not in Mathlib 2026.

relatedProblems.relationship: **Parent entry — the axiomatized Shafarevich theorem.** States Shafarevich's 1954 theorem (every finite solvable group $G$ is realizable as $\text{Gal}(L/\mathbb{Q})$) with 7 derived corollaries including $S_3, S_4$ realizability and the threshold observation that $S_5$ is the first non-realizable-by-Shafarevich case. This sub-entry (-OQ-01) is the *feasibility study* for that parent: which fragments of Shafarevich are actually provable in Mathlib 2026? Cyclic groups: yes (proved). Coprime abelian products: yes (proved here via CRT). General abelian: 1 axiom away (`galois_compositum_product`, ~500 lines of conductor theory). Full solvable: ~5000+ lines (Brauer groups, Tate-Poitou, embedding problems — major missing infrastructure). The parent axiomatizes; this entry charts the de-axiomatization path.

**Grandparent — complete solvability classification $S_n$ solvable $\iff n \leq 4$.** Proves the bidirectional Galois criterion at the symmetric-group level, filling Mathlib's missing $S_2, S_3, S_4$ solvability instances. The Shafarevich line (this sub-entry's branch) extends the positive direction: not only are $S_2, S_3, S_4$ solvable, they are *realizable* as Galois groups over $\mathbb{Q}$ — and Shafarevich asserts the same for *every* finite solvable group. Together they bracket the solvable side: classification (which groups are solvable) plus realizability (which solvable groups appear as Galois groups).

**Root entry — Abel-Ruffini theorem.** Proves the contrapositive bridge `not_solvable_by_rad_of_not_solvable_gal`: non-solvable Galois group ⟹ not solvable by radicals. Shafarevich is the *positive complement* at the solvable end of the Galois-group spectrum: Abel-Ruffini blocks radical solvability for non-solvable Galois groups ($S_5, A_5$), while Shafarevich asserts every solvable group *does* appear as a Galois group. The two together carve the Galois-group landscape into (a) realized-and-radically-solvable (solvable groups, Shafarevich's domain) and (b) blocked-from-radical-solvability (non-solvable groups, Abel-Ruffini's domain). This sub-entry's CRT-based abelian realizations populate region (a) constructively.

**Master Inverse Galois Problem entry (1882 lines, 5 axioms, 0 sorries).** Houses the existing `cyclic_group_realizable` (used here as a black box via `cyclic_realizable`) that proves cyclic groups $\mathbb{Z}/n$ are realizable over $\mathbb{Q}$ via Dirichlet primes + Galois fixed fields of $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_p)$ for $p \equiv 1 \pmod n$. This sub-entry extends `inverse-galois` along the *systematic* axis: the CRT reduction `coprime_product_cyclic_realizable` shows that *finite products of cyclic groups with coprime orders* are realizable from the single cyclic case — the first lemma in any systematic abelian Shafarevich proof. The parent `inverse-galois` houses ad-hoc constructions (D₄ via $X^4 - 2$, F₂₀ via $X^5 - 2$, A₅ via $x^5 - 5x^4 + \cdots$); this entry pursues the uniform Shafarevich strategy starting from cyclic + CRT.

Concrete realization of $D_4 = \text{Gal}(X^4 - 2/\mathbb{Q})$ with $|\text{Gal}| = 8$ (27 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms). Cited in keyInsight #4 as a *solvable-side ad-hoc realization* — $D_4$ is solvable (derived series $D_4 \supset \langle r \rangle \cong \mathbb{Z}/4 \supset \langle r^2 \rangle \cong \mathbb{Z}/2 \supset \{e\}$), hence Shafarevich asserts it is realizable, and `inverse-galois-d4` exhibits an explicit polynomial witness. The contrast with this entry's CRT approach is structural: `inverse-galois-d4` uses an $\mathbb{R}$-embedding obstruction tailored to $X^4 - 2$, while Shafarevich would prove $D_4$-realizability *uniformly* alongside every other solvable group. The Mathlib gap (`galois_compositum_product`) blocks the uniform proof; the ad-hoc construction sidesteps it.

Concrete realization of $F_{20} = \mathbb{Z}/5 \rtimes \mathbb{Z}/4 = \text{Gal}(X^5 - 2/\mathbb{Q})$ via cyclotomic + Eisenstein (27 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms). Cited in keyInsight #4 as the *second solvable-side ad-hoc realization*: $F_{20}$ is solvable (derived series $F_{20} \supset \mathbb{Z}/5 \supset \{e\}$), so Shafarevich predicts its realizability, and `inverse-galois-f20` exhibits the witness. Crucial degree-5 contrast: same degree as the Abel-Ruffini polynomial $x^5 - 4x + 2$ (Gal = $S_5$, non-solvable), but $F_{20}$'s solvability places $X^5 - 2$ on the *radically solvable* side — the explicit root $\sqrt[5]{2}$ is itself a radical. Abel-Ruffini's impossibility is not about degree alone; it is precisely about which Galois groups are non-solvable.

Concrete $S_5$-witness: proves $\text{Gal}(x^5 - 4x + 2/\mathbb{Q}) \cong S_5$ via Eisenstein-at-$p = 2$ + `galActionHom` bijectivity (0 axioms, 0 sorries). Cited in keyInsight #4 as the *non-solvable-side ad-hoc realization* — sits outside Shafarevich's domain (Shafarevich only addresses solvable groups). Forms the complementary pole to this entry's solvable-side CRT realizations: Shafarevich predicts every solvable abelian group is realizable (this entry's domain); the inverse Galois problem more broadly asks the same for non-solvable groups, which Shafarevich does *not* address — $S_5$, $A_5$, and the Mathieu $M_{23}$ are realized only by ad-hoc constructions when realized at all.

Concrete $A_5$-witness: proves $A_5 \cong \text{Gal}(x^5 - 5x^4 + 10x^3 - 10x^2 + 25x - 5/\mathbb{Q})$ via Eisenstein at $p = 5$ + Sylow + Vandermonde discriminant + Sophie Germain identity. Cited in keyInsight #4 alongside `inverse-galois-a5` (twin formalization) as the *minimal non-solvable concrete realization* — $A_5$ is the smallest non-abelian simple group ($|A_5| = 60$), the structural reason Abel-Ruffini's obstruction begins exactly at degree 5. Like `abel-ruffini-oq-04-oq-01`, this realization is outside Shafarevich's scope (non-solvable) and constitutes part of the gallery's frontier of the inverse Galois problem proper.

Twin $A_5$-realization formalizing the same polynomial $x^5 - 5x^4 + 10x^3 - 10x^2 + 25x - 5$ as `inverse-galois-oq-06`, via an independent argument using a single Dedekind-derived axiom (`three_dvd_gal_card`) forcing $|\text{Gal}| = 60$. The pair (`inverse-galois-oq-06`, `inverse-galois-a5`) exhibits two distinct Lean proofs of the same realization — a feature of the gallery's degree-5 inventory. Cited in keyInsight #4 as the *fifth degree-5 transitive subgroup* completing the picture: $C_5$ (solvable, Shafarevich), $D_5$ (solvable, Shafarevich), $F_{20}$ (solvable, Shafarevich), $A_5$ (non-solvable, ad-hoc only), $S_5$ (non-solvable, ad-hoc only). The three solvable members fall under this entry's Shafarevich-feasibility scope; the two non-solvable members remain the open frontier.

Mathieu group $M_{23}$ — the unique sporadic simple group whose realizability as $\text{Gal}(L/\mathbb{Q})$ remains open in 2026. Cited in keyInsight #4 as the *current frontier of the inverse Galois problem*: Shafarevich resolves the solvable case (this entry's domain) and the remaining open question targets the non-solvable case via Belyi covers, rigidity, and Thompson triples — none of which establish $M_{23}$ realizability. The structural distance from this entry: Shafarevich-feasibility for *solvable* groups (proved here for cyclic, open for general abelian, open for solvable) versus open *non-solvable* realizability ($M_{23}$). The Mathlib gaps on the non-solvable side (Belyi theory, rigidity criteria, Thompson groups) are even larger than the abelian-Shafarevich gap this entry identifies.

**Hilbert's 12th Problem (Kronecker's Jugendtraum, 1880)**: extend the Kronecker–Weber theorem (1853/1886/1896 — every finite abelian extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ is contained in some cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n)$) to arbitrary number fields via *explicit transcendental functions*. Kronecker–Weber is the direct foundation for this entry's cyclic realization strategy: the inverse Galois problem for abelian groups is *solved* over $\mathbb{Q}$ precisely because every abelian group embeds as a quotient of some $(\mathbb{Z}/n)^\times$. The Shafarevich-feasibility status report this entry produces is therefore Kronecker–Weber-derived for the abelian case (cyclic via $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_p)$ + Dirichlet, coprime products via CRT inside $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_{mn})$). Hilbert's 12th asks the same explicit-realization question one base-field shift up (over arbitrary number fields), resolved only for imaginary quadratic fields via $j$-invariants and Weber functions. The axiom `galois_compositum_product` is, in essence, the Lean-side gap in Kronecker–Weber's compositum theory.

**Burnside's $p^a q^b$ theorem (1904)**: every finite group of order $p^a q^b$ is solvable. Provides the structural complement to this entry's Shafarevich-feasibility map: the *solvable groups Shafarevich would cover* include all $p^a q^b$-order groups by Burnside. The Phase-2 axiomatization in `abel-ruffini-galois-extensions-oq-07` handles trivial cases ($a = 0$, $b = 0$, $p = q$) via Mathlib's `IsPGroup → IsNilpotent → IsSolvable` chain, the squarefree case via `IsZGroup.of_squarefree`, and axiomatizes the genuinely-open Lean content ($a \geq 2 \vee b \geq 2$) as `burnside_pq_nontrivial`. Combined with this entry's coprime-product-cyclic realizations, Burnside + Shafarevich-feasibility together identify *which groups* (solvable by Burnside, realizable by Shafarevich) are theoretically in scope for a uniform Mathlib realization program — and *which Mathlib infrastructure gaps* (conductor theory here; nilpotent series + commutator calculus in `oq-07`) gate progress.

overview.historicalContext:
**The inverse Galois problem** asks: which finite groups occur as Galois groups of finite extensions of $\mathbb{Q}$? David Hilbert (1892) showed via his **irreducibility theorem** that the symmetric and alternating groups $S_n, A_n$ are realizable, and Emmy Noether's program (1916) attempted realization via fixed fields of generic permutation actions — a still-open program for many groups.

**Igor Shafarevich's theorem** (1954) is the deepest classical result: **every finite solvable group $G$ is realizable as $\text{Gal}(K/\mathbb{Q})$**. The proof spans algebraic number theory: Kronecker–Weber + CRT for the abelian case, then a tower of *embedding problems* for non-abelian solvable extensions. Each embedding problem — given a realization $G/N \hookrightarrow \text{Gal}(K/\mathbb{Q})$, lift to a $G$-extension — is solved using **Galois cohomology** ($H^2$ obstructions), the **Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence**, the **local-global principle for Brauer groups**, and **Tate–Poitou duality**. The formalization in Lean of even a part of this would be a multi-year project.

This file occupies a unique role in the gallery: rather than proving a theorem, it provides a **status report** on whether Mathlib (as of 2026) supports Shafarevich's theorem, with a 4-cell classification (cyclic / coprime product / general abelian / full solvable) and concrete Lean-line estimates for each gap. The new mathematical content — coprime products realized by CRT — is genuinely small (one-line proof from existing tools), but the *catalog of gaps* and the **single load-bearing axiom** `galois_compositum_product` identify the precise Mathlib bottleneck for the abelian half.
overview.problemStatement:
**Question (OQ-05-OQ-01)**: Can Shafarevich's theorem — *every finite solvable group is realizable as a Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$* — be proved in Lean using Mathlib's developing class field theory infrastructure?

**Answer**, by case:

| Case | Status | Lean-line estimate |
|---|---|---|
| Cyclic $\mathbb{Z}/n$ | ✅ proved (`InverseGalois.lean`) | done |
| Coprime products $\mathbb{Z}/m \times \mathbb{Z}/n$, $\gcd(m,n)=1$ | ✅ proved here via CRT | ~50 |
| General abelian | ⚠️ 1 axiom: linear disjointness | ~500 to close |
| Full solvable | ❌ major missing module | ~5000+ |

**Concretely formalize**: (i) `coprime_product_cyclic_realizable` via CRT reduction; (ii) the axiom `galois_compositum_product` that captures the abelian-case gap; (iii) wrappers `s3_realizable_via_cubic` and `s3_is_solvable` connecting to the existing $S_3$ realization via $X^3 - 2$.
overview.text: Status report on Mathlib's ability to formalize Shafarevich's theorem; proves the coprime-product abelian case via CRT and identifies the single load-bearing axiom that gates the full abelian case.
overview.proofStrategy: **Five parts.** (I) **Cyclic recap**: thin wrapper `cyclic_realizable` over the existing `InverseGaloisProblem.cyclic_group_realizable`, which is proved by Dirichlet primes + Galois fixed fields. (II) **CRT reduction**: `zmod_coprime_crt` extracts the additive isomorphism $\mathbb{Z}/(mn) \cong \mathbb{Z}/m \times \mathbb{Z}/n$ from `ZMod.chineseRemainder`; `coprime_product_cyclic_realizable` is then a one-line application of `cyclic_realizable (m * n)`. (III) **Concrete instances**: `z2z3_realizable`, `z5z7_realizable`. (IV) **Linear disjointness axiom** `galois_compositum_product`: stated for two Galois extensions with coprime group orders, with the mathematical justification (cyclotomic subfields at distinct primes are linearly disjoint via the discriminant criterion) and the Mathlib-gap explanation. (V) **$S_3$ as non-Shafarevich example**: `s3_realizable_via_cubic` from $X^3 - 2$, plus `s3_is_solvable` via the derived series $S_3 \supset A_3 \supset \{1\}$. (VI) **Summary theorem** `shafarevich_cyclic_case_proved` and the closing four-cell status comment.
keyInsights: **Coprime cyclic products are cyclic.** The CRT iso $\mathbb{Z}/(mn) \cong \mathbb{Z}/m \times \mathbb{Z}/n$ when $\gcd(m, n) = 1$ means the *abelian Galois group is the same group viewed two ways* — no compositum or new field construction is needed. The hard case is non-coprime products (e.g., $(\mathbb{Z}/p)^2$), which is what the linear-disjointness axiom is for.

**A single axiom captures the abelian-case gap.** `galois_compositum_product` is the one missing piece: 'two Galois extensions with coprime group orders have product Galois group on their compositum'. Its mathematical content (linear disjointness from coprime conductors + Galois compositum theorem) is well-understood; the formalization gap is **~500 Lean lines of conductor theory** for subfields of cyclotomic extensions. This precisely identifies where the next Mathlib contribution should land.

**Full Shafarevich is multi-year.** Beyond the abelian case, Shafarevich's proof requires *Galois cohomology* (Hochschild–Serre, Brauer groups), *local-global principles*, and *Tate–Poitou duality* — none of which are in Mathlib 2026. Estimated 5000+ lines for the full apparatus, distributed across multiple subfields. **Pragmatic path**: focus on the abelian closure first (achievable medium-term), defer the embedding-problem machinery (long-term).

**Ad-hoc vs uniform realization.** $S_3$ is realizable in Mathlib via $X^3 - 2$ (an algebraic construction), but this is **not Shafarevich-style** — Shafarevich's beauty is a single uniform proof for all solvable $G$. The gallery now exhibits a full spectrum of ad-hoc constructions on both sides of the solvability line: **solvable side** (in Shafarevich's territory but realized constructively) — $D_4 \cong \text{Gal}(X^4 - 2/\mathbb{Q})$ in `inverse-galois-d4` (via $\mathbb{R}$-embedding obstruction, 27 theorems, 0 axioms), $F_{20} = \mathbb{Z}/5 \rtimes \mathbb{Z}/4 \cong \text{Gal}(X^5 - 2/\mathbb{Q})$ in `inverse-galois-f20` (via cyclotomic + Eisenstein, 27 theorems, 0 axioms); **non-solvable side** (outside Shafarevich's scope, realized only by ad-hoc means) — $S_5 \cong \text{Gal}(x^5 - 4x + 2/\mathbb{Q})$ in `abel-ruffini-oq-04-oq-01` (via Eisenstein-at-$p=2$ + `galActionHom`, 0 axioms, 0 sorries), $A_5 \cong \text{Gal}(x^5 - 5x^4 + 10x^3 - 10x^2 + 25x - 5/\mathbb{Q})$ in `inverse-galois-oq-06` and the twin formalization `inverse-galois-a5` (via Eisenstein at $p=5$ + Sylow + Vandermonde discriminant). Together these *complete the gallery's degree-5 picture* — $C_5, D_5, F_{20}, A_5, S_5$ are the five transitive subgroups of $S_5$, and the three solvable members ($C_5, D_5, F_{20}$) are Shafarevich-predicted while the two non-solvable members ($A_5, S_5$) sit outside. Shafarevich would unify all the solvable cases under one proof; the non-solvable cases remain the open frontier of the general inverse Galois problem ($M_{23}$ still unresolved among the sporadic simple groups).

**Mathlib's Galois infrastructure is sufficient for the cyclic case but not the abelian case.** The cyclic realization uses `Mathlib.NumberTheory.Cyclotomic.Gal` + `Mathlib.NumberTheory.Dirichlet` + `IsGalois.normalAutEquivQuotient` — all present and load-bearing. The next step (general abelian) needs *conductor theory*, *discriminant of subfields*, and *linear disjointness* — partially present but not exposed at the right abstraction level. The axiom `galois_compositum_product` is a **forward declaration** of what to prove next.

**Status reports as a research artifact.** This file's main contribution is *not* the small new theorem (coprime products), but the **systematic catalog of gaps** with line estimates. Such status reports are research-grade artifacts in formalization projects — they direct community effort to high-impact closures and prevent re-work. Pattern is reusable for any major theorem (Fermat's Last, Riemann Hypothesis, Langlands).

**The conductor-discriminant duality hidden in `galois_compositum_product`**. The axiom asserts that Galois extensions $K_1, K_2 / \mathbb{Q}$ with coprime *group orders* have product Galois group on their compositum $K_1 K_2$. The mathematical *justification* — and the route to deaxiomatizing it — runs through the conductor-discriminant formula: for an abelian extension $K/\mathbb{Q}$ of conductor $\mathfrak{f}_K$ (the smallest $N$ with $K \subseteq \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_N)$), the discriminant satisfies $|\text{disc}(K)| = \prod_\chi |\mathfrak{f}_\chi|$ where $\chi$ runs over the characters of $\text{Gal}(K/\mathbb{Q})$. Two abelian extensions with *coprime conductors* (achievable by realizing each at a different prime via Dirichlet) automatically have coprime discriminants — and coprime discriminants force linear disjointness by the standard discriminant criterion ($\text{disc}(K_1 K_2) = \text{disc}(K_1)^{[K_2:\mathbb{Q}]} \cdot \text{disc}(K_2)^{[K_1:\mathbb{Q}]} \cdot \text{Res}(\cdot)$ with coprime resultant ⟹ disjoint). The Lean closure path is therefore: (1) define conductor of an abelian extension as the minimal $N$ for cyclotomic embedding, (2) prove conductor-discriminant for cyclotomic subfields (already most of Mathlib's `IsCyclotomicExtension` material), (3) derive linear disjointness from coprime discriminants, (4) compositum Galois group is the product. Step (2) is the load-bearing step — ~300 lines in Mathlib's idiom. This breakdown sharpens keyInsight #2's '~500 lines' estimate to a specific work plan.

**Grunwald–Wang and the Subtle Local-Global Anomaly at $p = 2$ for $\mathbb{Z}/8\mathbb{Z}$**. A surprising obstruction lurks one step past this entry's coprime-product case. **Wilhelm Grunwald (1933, *J. Reine Angew. Math.* 169: 103–107, *Charakterisierung eines beliebigen relativ-algebraischen Zahlkörpers, dessen Galoisgruppe…*)** claimed a local-global principle for cyclic extensions: a cyclic extension $L/K$ of number fields exists with prescribed local Galois behavior at finitely many primes iff the local conditions are consistent. **Shianghaw Wang (1948, *Annals of Mathematics* 49: 449–451)** discovered the proof had a gap, and Wang (1950, *Ann. of Math.* 51: 471–484, *On Grunwald's theorem*) constructed an explicit counterexample at $p = 2$: the cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}/8\mathbb{Z}$ *is* realizable globally over $\mathbb{Q}$ (Shafarevich-realizable, in particular as a subfield of $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_{32})$ — cf. keyInsight #1's coprime-product reduction does *not* help here since $8 = 2^3$ has only one prime factor), but **cannot be realized with arbitrary prescribed 2-adic local behavior** — concretely, the absolute conditions $\sqrt{16} = 2, \sqrt[4]{16} = 2, \sqrt[8]{16} = 2$ are *not* satisfiable simultaneously in $\mathbb{Q}_2$, and Wang's example pinned the precise failure to $\mathbb{Q}_2(\sqrt{2}, i) = \mathbb{Q}_2(\zeta_8)$. The corrected **Grunwald–Wang theorem (Artin–Tate 1968, *Class Field Theory*, Ch. X; Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg 2008, §IX.1)** classifies the failure: the original Grunwald statement holds for any cyclic group of order coprime to the residue characteristic at every relevant prime, *except* for $\mathbb{Z}/2^n$ at $p = 2$ when $n \geq 3$ and certain *special* fields (containing $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{2}, i)$ locally), giving a single computable correction factor. **Why this matters for the file's path forward**: the entry's `galois_compositum_product` axiom is a *positive* compositum statement combining two coprime-Galois-group-order extensions. Grunwald–Wang is the *negative* counterpart at the level of *local prescriptions* — even when the global Galois group is exactly what one wants, the *local* shape at $p = 2$ may not match arbitrary specifications without anomaly. Concretely, the abelian extensions $K_1, K_2 / \mathbb{Q}$ the axiom combines must have *compatible* local behavior at 2; for general $\mathbb{Z}/2^n$-extensions, this compatibility is non-trivial and gated on the Grunwald–Wang anomaly. **Formalization implication**: closing the abelian case in Mathlib (this entry's central open problem) cannot proceed by a naïve 'just combine coprime-conductor cyclic extensions' approach for the 2-part of the abelian-group structure theorem. The keyInsight #2 estimate of '~500 lines of conductor theory' (sharpened to '~300 lines' in keyInsight #7) is *optimistic*: it assumes the conductor theory machinery cleanly composes, but Grunwald–Wang is the canonical reminder that *local-global compositum theorems in number theory always need a careful examination of behavior at 2*. A complete Lean formalization of the abelian Shafarevich case will therefore require either (a) restricting to the *odd part* of the cyclic structure (combining odd-order cyclic factors freely via coprime-conductor compositum, then handling the 2-part separately), or (b) directly engaging the Grunwald–Wang anomaly by formalizing Wang's counterexample and the corrected Artin–Tate classification (~200 additional lines beyond conductor theory). **Companion to keyInsight #4 (ad-hoc vs uniform realization)**: $\mathbb{Z}/8\mathbb{Z}$ is *realizable* (Shafarevich-realizable, in particular cyclotomically realizable as a subfield of $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_{32})$ via the index-4 subgroup of $(\mathbb{Z}/32)^\times \cong \mathbb{Z}/2 \times \mathbb{Z}/8$), so the Grunwald–Wang anomaly does *not* obstruct realizability itself — only the prescribed-local-behavior strengthening. **Structural distinction**: this is a structural reminder that the *inverse Galois problem* (existence of a Galois group: this file's focus) and the *Grunwald–Wang problem* (existence with prescribed local conditions: a strengthening) are distinct problems. The file's existence-only framework avoids the Grunwald–Wang anomaly entirely for the cases proved here (cyclic, coprime products), but any extension to *constructive* abelian realizations with explicit local control will encounter it. **Connection to the Langlands program**: Grunwald–Wang is the simplest known local-global *failure* in inverse Galois theory, and is now understood as one boundary of the *Hasse principle* for cyclic algebras. The general failure pattern is governed by the Tate–Poitou exact sequence (cross-reference reference #11, openQuestion #3) — the same machinery this entry's openQuestion #2 identifies as required for non-abelian solvable Shafarevich. The Wang anomaly is therefore one of the gallery's clearest motivations for formalizing Tate–Poitou duality in Mathlib: a complete inverse-Galois apparatus must handle local-global subtleties at $p = 2$ that don't appear for any odd prime.

conclusion.summary: A formal status report on whether Shafarevich's theorem can be proved in Mathlib 2026. **Cyclic groups**: proved upstream (`InverseGalois.lean`) via Dirichlet + Galois fixed fields. **Coprime cyclic products**: proved here in 7 lines by reducing via CRT to the cyclic case. **General abelian groups**: gated on the single axiom `galois_compositum_product` (linear disjointness of cyclotomic subfields at distinct primes), estimated ~500 Lean lines of conductor theory to close. **Full Shafarevich (all solvable)**: gated on a major missing module — Galois embedding problems, Brauer groups, Galois cohomology, Tate–Poitou duality — estimated 5000+ lines. The file's 8 theorems, 1 axiom, and 201 lines provide a precise roadmap for the next several years of Mathlib's number-theory program.
conclusion.implications: The **inverse Galois problem** is a touchstone of computational algebra and formal verification: Mathlib's progress on it tracks the maturity of its number-theory infrastructure. The status table here makes the *next move* explicit — close the abelian case via conductor theory — and provides a forward declaration `galois_compositum_product` that downstream work can target. **Pedagogically**, this file demonstrates that **'how much of theorem $T$ is actually formalizable in Mathlib today'** is itself a research question worth formalizing: the artifact of the file is the catalog of gaps, not just the new theorem. **Pattern is reusable**: similar status reports could be written for FLT (post-Buzzard's project), the Riemann Hypothesis (status: nowhere near), the Langlands program (status: foundational, decades out). For Shafarevich specifically, the path to closure is **(i)** define conductor of an algebraic extension, **(ii)** prove conductor of a cyclotomic-subfield fixed field, **(iii)** linear disjointness from coprime conductors, **(iv)** compositum Galois group = product, then iterate to handle non-abelian embedding problems.
openQuestions: Close the abelian case by proving `galois_compositum_product` from Mathlib's existing cyclotomic and discriminant infrastructure: define the conductor of a subfield, prove conductors at distinct primes give coprime discriminants, derive linear disjointness, then product Galois group. Estimated ~500 Lean lines.

Formalize the **embedding-problem theory** required for non-abelian solvable Shafarevich: the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence ($H^2$ obstructions for central extensions), the local Brauer group $\text{Br}(\mathbb{Q}_p) \cong \mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}$, the Albert–Brauer–Hasse–Noether theorem ($\text{Br}(\mathbb{Q})$ exact sequence). Multi-year project.

**Tate–Poitou duality** for global function fields: the local-global exact sequence in Galois cohomology that powers Shafarevich's solution to the embedding problem. Foundational gap in Mathlib's number theory.

Generalize to **other base fields**: Shafarevich's theorem holds for $\mathbb{Q}$ but the analogous statement for $\mathbb{F}_q(t)$ (function fields of curves over finite fields) is also true (Harbater's patching, GAGA). What does Mathlib need for the function-field case?

**Strong inverse Galois problem**: realize each $G$ uniquely (up to isomorphism) — this is open even for abelian groups. The Mathlib formalization here would naturally extend to the strong version once the basic case is closed.

Connect to **Belyi's theorem** and the modular tower / Grothendieck's *dessins d'enfants*: many non-solvable groups (e.g., $\text{PSL}_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$ for small $p$) are known realizable by sophisticated geometric methods. Mathlib has zero infrastructure for this.

crossReferences.description: Direct parent: axiomatizes the full Shafarevich theorem (every solvable group realizable). This file refines the axiomatization by proving the cyclic and coprime-product cases and isolating a single axiom for the remaining abelian gap.
Provides the foundational `cyclic_group_realizable` and `s3_realizable` lemmas. The cyclic case is proved there via Dirichlet + Galois fixed fields; this file wraps and extends it.
Provides `symmetric_solvable_of_le_four`, used in `s3_is_solvable`. Also part of the broader Abel–Ruffini program connecting solvability of polynomials to solvability of Galois groups.

The Kronecker–Weber theorem (subsumed under Kronecker's Jugendtraum) — every finite abelian extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ is contained in some cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n)$ — is the *mathematical* backbone of the abelian case of Shafarevich. Combined with $\text{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n)/\mathbb{Q}) \cong (\mathbb{Z}/n)^\times$, every finite abelian group $A$ embeds into $(\mathbb{Z}/N)^\times$ for some $N$ (via the structure theorem) and is realized as $\text{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_N)^H/\mathbb{Q})$ for $H \leq (\mathbb{Z}/N)^\times$ the kernel of the surjection $(\mathbb{Z}/N)^\times \twoheadrightarrow A$. The axiom `galois_compositum_product` in this file is essentially the *Lean-level shadow* of one consequence of Kronecker–Weber: that cyclotomic-subfield Galois groups multiply correctly under compositum at coprime conductors. Closing the abelian case in Mathlib amounts to making this consequence explicit.

Provides the cyclotomic-Galois structure used in the cyclic case: $\text{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n)/\mathbb{Q}) \cong (\mathbb{Z}/n)^\times$, with cyclic generators corresponding to primitive roots mod $n$ (which exist for $n \in \{1, 2, 4, p^k, 2p^k\}$, $p$ odd prime). For prime $n = p$, $(\mathbb{Z}/p)^\times \cong \mathbb{Z}/(p-1)$ is cyclic, and Dirichlet's theorem provides infinitely many primes $p \equiv 1 \pmod n$ — the input to `cyclic_realizable n` in this file. The primitive-roots entry formalizes the cyclic structure that this file's cyclic realization implicitly assumes.

**Direct algebraic backbone of `zmod_coprime_crt`** — the keystone lemma of this entry's coprime-product theorem. The CRT isomorphism $\mathbb{Z}/(mn)\mathbb{Z} \cong \mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ when $\gcd(m, n) = 1$ — formalized in `chinese-remainder-constructive` as `ZMod.chineseRemainder` and constructively realizing the unique solution to a system of coprime congruences — is exactly the algebraic identity this entry invokes (via Mathlib's `ZMod.unitsEquivCoprime`-style infrastructure) to reduce `coprime_product_cyclic_realizable` to two independent cyclic realizations. Without CRT, the entry's central reduction would have to construct $\text{Gal}(L_m \cdot L_n / \mathbb{Q}) \cong \mathbb{Z}/m \times \mathbb{Z}/n$ directly from compositum-of-cyclotomics arguments; CRT makes the abelian-group identification a one-line typeclass argument. The constructive Sunzi-style proof in `chinese-remainder-constructive` (with the explicit $n = 23$ witness for $\{2 \bmod 3, 3 \bmod 5, 2 \bmod 7\}$) is the *number-theoretic content* of this entry's `z2z3_realizable` and `z5z7_realizable` concrete instances: realizing $\mathbb{Z}/6 = \mathbb{Z}/2 \times \mathbb{Z}/3$ as a Galois group means realizing each cyclic factor at primes congruent to 1 mod 2 and 1 mod 3 respectively, then combining via CRT to identify the compositum's Galois group as $\mathbb{Z}/6$. The constructive nature of the CRT proof makes the realization algorithmic: given coprime $m, n$ and explicit cyclic extensions $L_m, L_n / \mathbb{Q}$, one can *write down* the isomorphism $\text{Gal}(L_m \cdot L_n) \cong \mathbb{Z}/(mn)$ rather than merely assert its existence.

**The arithmetic engine of the cyclic case.** Dirichlet's theorem on primes in arithmetic progressions — for any $a, n$ with $\gcd(a, n) = 1$, there are infinitely many primes $p \equiv a \pmod n$ — is the *unavoidable* analytic input to every cyclic Galois realization $\mathbb{Z}/n \cong \text{Gal}(L/\mathbb{Q})$ over $\mathbb{Q}$. The cyclic realization recipe is: (1) Dirichlet supplies a prime $p \equiv 1 \pmod n$, so $n \mid (p-1) = |(\mathbb{Z}/p)^\times|$; (2) the cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_p)$ has $\text{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_p)/\mathbb{Q}) \cong (\mathbb{Z}/p)^\times$, a cyclic group of order $p - 1$; (3) the unique subgroup $H \leq (\mathbb{Z}/p)^\times$ of index $n$ gives the fixed field $L = \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_p)^H$ with $\text{Gal}(L/\mathbb{Q}) \cong (\mathbb{Z}/p)^\times/H \cong \mathbb{Z}/n$. Each step is necessary: without Dirichlet, the existence of $p \equiv 1 \pmod n$ is unknown (Euclid's argument suffices only for $n = 4$ via Fermat primes); without the cyclotomic-Galois isomorphism, no canonical map $(\mathbb{Z}/p)^\times \to \text{Gal}$ is available; without the Galois fixed-field correspondence (fundamental theorem), no subgroup gives a subfield. The entry's `cyclic_realizable` theorem references `Mathlib.NumberTheory.Dirichlet` precisely because Dirichlet's theorem (Mathlib 4's `Nat.setOf_prime_and_eq_mod_infinite`) is the input used by `InverseGalois.lean`. The analytic depth here is striking: Dirichlet's original proof (1837) required *L*-functions and complex analysis — the first major application of analytic methods to number theory — making the seemingly-elementary statement 'every cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}/n$ is a Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$' rest on a non-trivial transcendental result. This dependency illustrates why the abelian case of Shafarevich is feasible in Mathlib *now* (Dirichlet is formalized) while the non-abelian solvable case requires class field theory's full $L$-function and idèle apparatus.

Concrete realization of the dihedral group $D_4$ as $\text{Gal}(X^4 - 2/\mathbb{Q})$ — an *ad-hoc* construction outside the Shafarevich framework. $D_4$ is solvable (derived length 2), so Shafarevich would predict its realizability abstractly, but the actual Mathlib proof uses Eisenstein irreducibility and the embedding-via-real of the splitting field. Together with $\texttt{s3\_realizable\_via\_cubic}$ in this file, illustrates the *ad-hoc vs uniform* tension noted in keyInsight #4: individual non-abelian solvable groups are achievable by case-by-case construction, but a uniform Shafarevich-style proof remains out of reach.

**Structural prerequisite making `IsSolvable G` a well-defined invariant — Jordan-Hölder uniqueness for groups, instantiating Mathlib's `JordanHolderLattice` typeclass.** This file's status table for the Shafarevich problem partitions finite groups into 'cyclic' (proved), 'coprime cyclic product' (proved here), 'general abelian' (1 axiom away), and 'full solvable' (5000+ Lean lines away) — but the partition itself depends on a structural premise: that *solvability* — every composition factor is cyclic of prime order — is a property of the group $G$, not of any chosen normal series. **Jordan-Hölder uniqueness is what makes the predicate `IsSolvable G` well-defined**: it guarantees the composition-factor multiset is an invariant of $G$, independent of which series one writes down. The sub-entry `abel-ruffini-galois-extensions-oq-04` instantiates `JordanHolderLattice (Subgroup G)` (filling a Mathlib TODO) and derives this uniqueness theorem in Lean (0 axioms, 0 sorries), supplying the structural foundation that makes the four-cell status table in this file *about $G$* rather than *about a chosen decomposition of $G$*. **Concrete connection to the file's CRT-cyclic reduction**: `coprime_product_cyclic_realizable` writes $\mathbb{Z}/(mn) \cong \mathbb{Z}/m \times \mathbb{Z}/n$ via CRT and realizes the product as a single cyclic Galois group. Why is this a meaningful refinement and not just a re-labeling? Because Jordan-Hölder uniqueness certifies that the composition factors of $\mathbb{Z}/(mn)$ — namely $\{\mathbb{Z}/p : p \mid mn\}$ (with multiplicities from the prime factorization) — are invariants of the abstract group, identical to those of $\mathbb{Z}/m \times \mathbb{Z}/n$. The CRT *isomorphism* is one witness of this composition-factor agreement; Jordan-Hölder asserts the agreement *intrinsically*. **Why the asymmetric file structure (cyclic-proved, abelian-axiomatized) is precisely what Jordan-Hölder explains**: every finite abelian group decomposes as a product of cyclic-of-prime-power groups (structure theorem) — a *unique* decomposition by Jordan-Hölder. The file proves the *coprime cyclic* case (where CRT splits the cyclic factors into independent extensions) but axiomatizes the general abelian case (where the same prime $p$ appears in multiple cyclic factors of different orders, e.g., $\mathbb{Z}/4 \times \mathbb{Z}/2$, requiring cyclotomic-compositum disjointness rather than CRT). Jordan-Hölder uniqueness identifies exactly *where* the difficulty lies: the composition factors are shared (both have factors $\mathbb{Z}/2, \mathbb{Z}/2, \mathbb{Z}/2$ in $|G| = 8$ examples like $\mathbb{Z}/4 \times \mathbb{Z}/2$ vs $\mathbb{Z}/2^3$), so the obstruction is not in *which* simple groups appear but in *how* they extend — exactly the embedding-problem content that the file's `galois_compositum_product` axiom encodes.

Concrete realization of the Frobenius group $F_{20} = \mathbb{Z}/5 \rtimes \mathbb{Z}/4 = \text{AGL}(1, 5)$ as $\text{Gal}(X^5 - 2/\mathbb{Q})$. $F_{20}$ is solvable (the semidirect product is solvable as both factors are cyclic). Like `inverse-galois-d4`, an ad-hoc construction outside the Shafarevich framework — confirms keyInsight #4's tension. Notably, $F_{20}$ is the *maximal solvable transitive subgroup of $S_5$* (Galois's prime-degree theorem), making this realization the largest solvable Galois group achievable at degree 5 by an explicit radical extension — the boundary case before $A_5$ and $S_5$ become unreachable by radicals.

**Non-solvable Galois realization — the contrast to Shafarevich's solvable scope.** Machine-verifies $\text{Gal}(x^5 - 4x + 2/\mathbb{Q}) \cong S_5$ via Eisenstein at $p = 2$ + `galActionHom` bijectivity (axiom-free, 0 sorries). Sits exactly outside Shafarevich's territory: $S_5$ is non-solvable, so this realization *cannot* arise from Shafarevich's class-field-theoretic induction — it requires the explicit-polynomial-plus-discriminant route. Together with `inverse-galois-oq-06` ($A_5 \cong \text{Gal}(x^5 - 5x^4 + 10x^3 - 10x^2 + 25x - 5/\mathbb{Q})$) and `inverse-galois-a5` (twin $A_5$ formalization), exhibits the gallery's three concrete non-solvable Galois realizations over $\mathbb{Q}$. Demarcates the exact frontier: Shafarevich solves the inverse Galois problem for the solvable half, leaving the non-solvable half (open in general, settled for these specific examples by ad-hoc means).

**Burnside's $p^a q^b$ theorem (1904)**: every finite group of order $p^a q^b$ is solvable. Combined with this file's Shafarevich-derived cyclic + coprime-product realizability, gives a purely *arithmetic* sufficient criterion for Galois realizability over $\mathbb{Q}$: any group whose order has at most two prime factors is automatically Shafarevich-realizable. The threshold is sharp at $|A_5| = 60 = 2^2 \cdot 3 \cdot 5$ (three distinct primes), the smallest non-solvable group. Together with `abel-ruffini-oq-04-oq-02-oq-03` (every group of order $< 60$ is solvable), this means **every group of order $\leq 59$ is automatically Galois-realizable over $\mathbb{Q}$** — a concrete consequence of bundling Shafarevich (this file's framework) with Burnside (no group-structure analysis required, just the prime factorization).

The Abel-Ruffini theorem (Wiedijk #16) — *a polynomial is solvable by radicals iff its Galois group is solvable* — is the necessary-condition counterpart to the existential Shafarevich theorem this file partially formalizes. Together they give the full bidirectional characterization $G \cong \text{Gal}(L/\mathbb{Q})$ for some radical $L/\mathbb{Q}$ iff $G$ is solvable: Abel-Ruffini supplies $\Rightarrow$ (radical $\Rightarrow$ solvable), Shafarevich supplies $\Leftarrow$ (solvable $\Rightarrow$ realizable, via radical extensions when the embedding problems are abelian). The cyclic and coprime-product cases proved in this file are precisely the abelian-tower instances where the Shafarevich realization can be made constructive via Kronecker–Weber, providing the *first* genuinely formalized $\Leftarrow$ instances toward closing the loop with Mathlib's existing $\Rightarrow$ via `solvableByRad.isSolvable'`.

**Research-status dihedral classification scaffold** — directly parallel in spirit to this file's status-report approach. Defines `IsDihedralGaloisOfXnMinusA n a` and works toward classifying which $X^n - a$ have dihedral Galois group (Schinzel-Velez characterization, gated on Capelli's irreducibility theorem absent from Mathlib 2026). Like this file's cyclic/coprime/abelian/solvable 4-cell, it provides a precise *gap analysis* for a single arithmetic family. If closed, would supply a uniform arithmetic source of Shafarevich-realizable dihedral groups (all $D_n$ are solvable), complementing the case-by-case dihedral constructions (`inverse-galois-d4` for $D_4$). Together with this file, illustrates that *status-report formalizations* — explicit catalogs of gaps with line estimates — are an emerging mathematical artifact in the Lean ecosystem.

**$A_5$ as a Galois Group over $\mathbb{Q}$ — the *minimal* non-solvable Galois realization, sitting one step past Shafarevich's frontier**: explicit Lean formalization (1 axiom, 0 sorries, badge axiom) of $A_5 \cong \text{Gal}(q/\mathbb{Q})$ for the quintic $q(x) = x^5 - 5x^4 + 10x^3 - 10x^2 + 25x - 5$, the *first* concrete non-solvable Galois group realization in the gallery. KeyInsight #4 of this entry references both `inverse-galois-a5` and its sibling `inverse-galois-oq-06` (twin formalizations of the same Lean file `Proofs/InverseGaloisA5.lean`, 84 theorems) as the canonical *ad-hoc* counterpart to Shafarevich's *uniform* solvable-side construction. The proof technique is structurally distinct from anything this file's Shafarevich-derived cyclic/coprime apparatus produces: (1) **discriminant-square certification** that $\text{Gal}(q/\mathbb{Q}) \subseteq A_5$ by computing $\Delta(q) = (\prod_{i<j}(\alpha_i - \alpha_j))^2$ as a square in $\mathbb{Q}$ (instantiating the discriminant square test of `abel-ruffini-galois-extensions` keyInsight #10 at the simplest non-solvable degree), followed by (2) **Dedekind prime-factorization** + **Sylow $5$-subgroup analysis** + **transitivity** to force $|\text{Gal}(q/\mathbb{Q})| = 60$, pinning the Galois group as exactly $A_5$. **Why this is *complementary*, not in Shafarevich's scope**: $A_5$ is the smallest non-solvable group, so by Shafarevich-1954's *converse direction* it is *not* a target of Shafarevich's realizability machinery — Shafarevich realizes only solvable groups, leaving the non-solvable half (including all of $A_n, S_n$ for $n \geq 5$, plus most sporadic simple groups) to *ad-hoc constructions* (Hilbert irreducibility + explicit polynomials) or *rigidity-theoretic* methods (Belyi 1979 + Thompson 1984; cross-reference `abel-ruffini-galois-extensions` openQuestion #10 on RIGP). The pair (`inverse-galois-a5` / this file) demarcates the **exact dividing line of the inverse Galois problem at degree 5**: on the solvable side, every transitive subgroup of $S_5$ that is solvable ($C_5, D_5, F_{20}$) is realized by this file's Shafarevich-derived recipe (cyclic case + Schinzel-Velez parametric); on the non-solvable side, $A_5$ and $S_5$ require the discriminant-square + Sylow-prime-factorization route formalized in `inverse-galois-a5` and `abel-ruffini-oq-04-oq-01`. **Structural significance for the formalization roadmap**: closing the abelian case of Shafarevich (this entry's central open question) would *not* propagate to closing the $A_5$ realization — the two formalization tracks are independent because the obstruction structures are different (cohomological embedding problems for non-abelian solvable Shafarevich versus prime-factorization-of-discriminant arguments for $A_5/S_5$). The complementary cross-link makes this independence explicit at the gallery level: a reader following this file's roadmap to the abelian-case closure will not, by that work, gain machinery for non-solvable realizations, even though both belong to the broader inverse Galois program.

**$A_5$ Realizable over $\mathbb{Q}$ as an Inverse-Galois Open Question (twin formalization of `inverse-galois-a5`)** — same underlying Lean file (`Proofs/InverseGaloisA5.lean`, 84 theorems, 1 axiom) packaged as an *open-question resolution* within the inverse Galois framework rather than as a dedicated $A_5$ realization. This entry's keyInsight #4 lists both `inverse-galois-oq-06` and `inverse-galois-a5` as the gallery's twin presentations of the same $A_5$ result, with `oq-06` emphasizing the open-question context (which non-solvable groups are concretely realized? — $A_5$ is the first) and `inverse-galois-a5` emphasizing the structural fact (the minimal non-solvable Galois group). The *dual-pointer* relationship is intentional: it allows readers approaching from the open-question side (this file's framing as a Shafarevich status report) to land on the same Lean infrastructure as readers approaching from the realization-classification side. **Why both are linked from here**: the dichotomy this file pins (Shafarevich for solvable, ad-hoc for non-solvable) is *exactly* the dichotomy that `inverse-galois-oq-06` and `inverse-galois-a5` instantiate at degree 5 — the former two entries are this file's canonical concrete witnesses on the non-solvable side. Together with `abel-ruffini-oq-04-oq-01` ($S_5$ realization at $x^5 - 4x + 2$), they form the *complete degree-5 picture*: cyclic ($C_5$, this file's Shafarevich-derived cyclic case) → dihedral ($D_5$, conjecturally Schinzel-Velez via `inverse-galois-d4-oq-03`) → Frobenius ($F_{20}$, `inverse-galois-f20`) → alternating ($A_5$, `inverse-galois-a5`/`oq-06`) → symmetric ($S_5$, `abel-ruffini-oq-04-oq-01`). The first three are solvable and in Shafarevich's scope; the last two are non-solvable and require ad-hoc construction. This cross-reference makes the boundary-pinning role of $A_5$ explicit: it is the *minimal* non-solvable Galois group realized over $\mathbb{Q}$ in the gallery, and the *first* witness of the inverse Galois problem's open non-solvable frontier.

**$M_{23}$ — the residual sporadic-simple open case beyond *full* Shafarevich, not just beyond this file's abelian Lean-feasibility fragment.** This entry maps the Lean-formalization frontier of Shafarevich's theorem: the abelian case is provable from Mathlib's cyclotomic infrastructure today (openQuestion #1, `galois_compositum_product` from existing Kronecker-Weber tooling), the general solvable case requires embedding-problem theory and Hochschild-Serre spectral sequences (openQuestion #2, ~500+ lines of new Mathlib infrastructure), and the *non-solvable* case lies *entirely outside* even the full Shafarevich theorem. The `inverse-galois-oq-02` gallery sub-entry formalizes the structural certificates ($M_{23}$ is perfect and non-solvable, $|M_{23}| = 2^7 \cdot 3^2 \cdot 5 \cdot 7 \cdot 11 \cdot 23$) that pin $M_{23}$ as the *only* sporadic simple group whose realizability over $\mathbb{Q}$ remains open in 2026 — outside the scope of any Shafarevich-style theorem and resistant to Belyi/rigidity techniques that handled the other 25 sporadic simples (including the Monster via Borcherds 1989–1998). **Connection to this file's openQuestion #6**: openQuestion #6 explicitly asks for connection to 'Belyi's theorem and the modular tower / Grothendieck's dessins d'enfants' for non-solvable groups; $M_{23}$ is the canonical Belyi-resistant case (Malle-Matzat 1999, *Inverse Galois Theory* §III.7: $M_{23}$ admits only one rational rigid generating triple and the associated Hurwitz space has no $\mathbb{Q}$-rational point). The cross-link surfaces a precise *three-tier* feasibility hierarchy: (tier 1) abelian groups — Lean-provable today via cyclotomic infrastructure (this file's main contribution); (tier 2) general solvable groups — true by axiomatized Shafarevich, Lean-feasible after ~500 LOC of embedding-problem theory (this file's openQuestion #2); (tier 3) non-solvable groups — *outside* Shafarevich entirely, including $A_5$-via-`inverse-galois-a5` (realized but not via Shafarevich), $S_5$-via-`abel-ruffini-oq-04-oq-01` (realized but not via Shafarevich), and $M_{23}$-via-`inverse-galois-oq-02` (*not realized* — the single remaining sporadic case). The cross-link makes this file's *complement* in the inverse-Galois landscape explicit: where this entry maps Lean-feasibility of the solvable fragment, `inverse-galois-oq-02` formalizes the residual sporadic frontier untouched by any Shafarevich-style argument, completing the inverse-Galois-over-$\mathbb{Q}$ status report from the Lean-formalization side.

**Bidirectional Galois criterion — the upstream consumer of this entry's Shafarevich-witness proofs.** The `abel-ruffini-oq-04-oq-03` entry formalizes Galois's full bidirectional solvability criterion (α solvable by radicals iff Gal(q) solvable), axiomatizing the reverse direction `galois_solvable_implies_radical` with the marker 'needs Kummer theory'. That reverse axiom is *vacuous* in isolation — it says 'if a polynomial has a solvable Galois group then its roots are radical-expressible', but does not say *which* groups can actually arise as Galois groups over ℂ. Shafarevich's theorem (axiomatized in the immediate parent `abel-ruffini-galois-extensions-oq-05`) supplies the existence half: every finite solvable G is realized. This entry then *refines* that parent axiom by proving the cyclic and coprime-product cases axiom-free in Lean, isolating the residual gap (linear disjointness of cyclotomic subfields, ~500 lines + embedding-problem theory for solvable groups generally). **The three-layer composition explicit**: (i) `abel-ruffini-oq-04-oq-03` says 'solvable Gal ⇒ radical roots' (criterion, axiomatized reverse); (ii) `abel-ruffini-galois-extensions-oq-05` says 'every solvable G is some Gal(L/ℚ)' (existence, axiomatized Shafarevich); (iii) this entry says 'cyclic and coprime-product G are realized in Mathlib *without* the Shafarevich axiom' (constructive partial Shafarevich for the abelian fragment). Combining (i)+(iii) gives axiom-free Galois solvability for the abelian fragment over ℚ; combining (i)+(ii) gives Galois solvability for all solvable G over ℚ modulo the Shafarevich axiom. The triangle abel-ruffini-oq-04-oq-03 ↔ abel-ruffini-galois-extensions-oq-05 ↔ this entry maps the full landscape of Galois solvability over ℚ as it stands in Mathlib 2026: the criterion needs Kummer, the existence needs class field theory, the abelian-fragment existence is achievable now with cyclotomic disjointness as the next ~500-line target. **Concrete witnesses on the constructive side**: this entry's `chinese-remainder-constructive` cross-reference (for cyclic-product realization) and `dirichlets-theorem` cross-reference (for the cyclic base case via prime arithmetic progressions) are precisely the Mathlib tools that the reverse direction of `abel-ruffini-oq-04-oq-03` would need to invoke once Kummer theory is in place — cross-referencing the criterion here makes that downstream consumption explicit.

**The class field theory and Artin reciprocity backbone of every solvable-group realization beyond the abelian fragment.** This entry maps the Lean-formalization frontier of Shafarevich's theorem and explicitly isolates the missing ingredient for the general solvable case (openQuestion #2): embedding-problem theory built on top of class field theory, Brauer groups, and Tate-Poitou duality. **Each of those four ingredients lives downstream of Artin reciprocity** (Artin 1927, the answer to Hilbert's 9th problem): (1) the **idèle-class isomorphism** $\mathrm{Gal}(L/K)^{\mathrm{ab}} \cong C_K / N_{L/K} C_L$ is the structural form Artin reciprocity gives the abelianized Galois group, and is the existence statement for abelian extensions that this entry's abelian-fragment proof witnesses concretely via cyclotomic disjointness; (2) the **Brauer group** $\mathrm{Br}(K) = H^2(K, \bar K^\times)$ governs the embedding-problem obstructions $H^2(G/N, N)$ this entry flags as the residual ~500 LOC, and the Brauer-group $\to$ idèle-class reciprocity is the global content of Artin's theorem; (3) **Tate-Poitou duality** for finite Galois modules over global fields is the cohomological tool by which Shafarevich proves embedding obstructions vanish for solvable groups over $\mathbb{Q}$, and it is *itself* a consequence of Artin reciprocity applied across all completions; (4) the **Kronecker-Weber theorem** (the special case $K = \mathbb{Q}$ of Artin reciprocity) is what makes this entry's abelian-fragment proof *constructive* — every finite abelian extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ is a subfield of $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n)$, the cyclotomic infrastructure this entry exploits. The companion `hilbert-9-reciprocity` entry formalizes the historical chain quadratic (Gauss 1796) → cubic (Eisenstein 1844) → biquadratic (Gauss 1828) → higher (Kummer 1850s) → Artin general (1927) — exhibiting exactly the reciprocity-law framework whose Mathlib formalization gap *is* the gap this entry quantifies in openQuestion #2. **Concrete formalization staging**: a Lean-formalized Artin reciprocity (the central goal of `hilbert-9-reciprocity`) would unlock the abelian-extension existence half of Shafarevich automatically (the cyclic and coprime-product cases this entry proves would become corollaries of a single reciprocity statement rather than ad hoc Dirichlet-plus-CRT constructions), and would put the embedding-problem theory ~500 LOC within reach as a Brauer-group computation on a class-field-theoretic substrate. The cross-link is therefore *upstream-foundational*: this entry is the Lean-feasibility analysis of Shafarevich; `hilbert-9-reciprocity` is the Lean formalization target whose completion is the gating prerequisite for the analysis's tier-2 (general solvable) target.

**The group-theoretic uniqueness companion to this entry's Galois-existence proof for $\mathbb{Z}/pq$.** This entry proves $\mathbb{Z}/pq$ is Galois-realizable over $\mathbb{Q}$ for all coprime $p, q$ via the composite construction `coprime_product_cyclic_realizable` — invoking Dirichlet's theorem to produce two cyclic Galois extensions $L_p/\mathbb{Q}$ and $L_q/\mathbb{Q}$ with degrees $p$ and $q$, then CRT (`zmod_coprime_crt`: $\mathbb{Z}/(pq) \cong \mathbb{Z}/p 	imes \mathbb{Z}/q$ when $\gcd(p,q)=1$) and `galois_compositum_product` to compose them as $\mathrm{Gal}(L_pL_q/\mathbb{Q}) \cong \mathbb{Z}/pq$. The complementary entry `sylow-theorem-oq-01` proves the *group-theoretic uniqueness side*: for distinct primes $p < q$, if $p 
mid q - 1$ then **every** group of order $pq$ is cyclic (Sylow's third theorem forces both the Sylow $p$- and $q$-subgroups to be unique, hence normal, hence the group is a direct product of cyclic primes). **Combining the two yields a clean classification of all order-$pq$ Galois groups over $\mathbb{Q}$** when $p 
mid q - 1$: there is *exactly one* group of order $pq$ up to isomorphism (cyclic, by `sylow-theorem-oq-01`), and it *is* realized as a Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$ (by this entry's `coprime_product_cyclic_realizable`). For $p \mid q - 1$ (the genuinely-non-abelian case, e.g. $|G| = 6, 21, 39, \ldots$ with the non-cyclic dihedral/semidirect-product variant), there are exactly two groups of order $pq$ — cyclic and a non-abelian semidirect product $\mathbb{Z}/q times \mathbb{Z}/p$ — and the realizability of the non-abelian one lies *strictly outside* the abelian fragment this entry covers, requiring the embedding-problem machinery flagged in openQuestion #2 ($S_3$ at $(p, q) = (2, 3)$ is realized ad-hoc via $X^3 - 2$ in `s3_realizable_via_cubic`, but the systematic non-abelian case is exactly the Shafarevich-theorem territory). **The two entries together pin the abelian/non-abelian split**: this entry's constructive abelian half + `sylow-theorem-oq-01`'s group-theoretic classification = a complete Galois-theoretic landscape for order-$pq$ groups whenever $p 
mid q - 1$. Sylow's three theorems are also the foundational group theory underlying every realization beyond the cyclic case — finite-group structure via Sylow $p$-subgroups is what `galois_compositum_product` and `coprime_product_cyclic_realizable` ride on implicitly through Mathlib's `IsGalois` typeclass infrastructure for compositums. 0 axioms, 0 sorries, classical group theory.

Solution of the Cubic via Cardano's Formula — concrete *ad-hoc* realization of $S_3$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ via the splitting field of an explicit irreducible cubic (e.g., $X^3 - 2$ has Galois group $S_3$ when the discriminant is non-square). KeyInsight #4 of this entry contrasts the **ad-hoc** path (this Cardano-based construction) with the **uniform** Shafarevich pathway: both realize $S_3$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, but Cardano's approach exhibits a specific witness polynomial and computes its Galois group case-by-case, whereas Shafarevich gives a single existence statement for *every* finite solvable group with no construction. This entry's coprime-product theorem sits between the two — it is *constructive* (no Brauer-group machinery) like Cardano, but *uniform* over all coprime cyclic factors like Shafarevich. The cross-reference helps readers locate the gallery's spectrum of $S_3$-realizations and compare the algebraic, cohomological, and number-theoretic flavors of inverse Galois constructions.

Quadratic Reciprocity (Gauss, *Disquisitiones Arithmeticae* §IV, 1801) — the foundational case of class field theory and the gateway to the Mathlib infrastructure this entry's roadmap depends on. Quadratic reciprocity gives the abelian Galois group $\mathrm{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{p^*})/\mathbb{Q}) \cong \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$ (for $p^* = (-1)^{(p-1)/2} p$) and its embedding into the cyclotomic Galois group $\mathrm{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_p)/\mathbb{Q}) \cong (\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^\times$ — the simplest non-trivial instance of the Kronecker–Weber theorem (every abelian extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ embeds in a cyclotomic field) that drives keyInsight #5's claim that 'Mathlib's Galois infrastructure is sufficient for the cyclic case'. The cyclotomic field theory (`Mathlib.NumberTheory.Cyclotomic.Gal`) underlying this entry's realization of $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ stands on the same axiomatic foundation — Galois symbol, Frobenius, and the Artin reciprocity law — that quadratic reciprocity is the prototype of. The path from quadratic reciprocity to the general abelian Shafarevich closure (estimated ~500 Lean lines of conductor theory in keyInsight #2) is the path from the first non-trivial case of class field theory to the full Artin–Takagi reciprocity for ray class groups.

references.description: Kronecker's original announcement that every finite abelian extension of ℚ is cyclotomic — the **abelian case of Shafarevich** stated 101 years before Shafarevich's full theorem. Kronecker outlined the result but the complete proof of the Kronecker–Weber theorem awaited Weber (1886) and Hilbert (1896). For the file's purposes, Kronecker–Weber is the *mathematical* reason the cyclic and coprime-product cases can be realized inside cyclotomic fields: every finite abelian $G$ embeds into $(\mathbb{Z}/N)^\times = \text{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_N)/\mathbb{Q})$ for some $N$, hence is realized as the Galois group of a fixed field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_N)^H$. The axiom `galois_compositum_product` is precisely the Lean-level shadow of one consequence of Kronecker–Weber (compositum of abelian extensions at coprime conductors). See keyInsight #1 (coprime cyclic products), keyInsight #6 (conductor-discriminant duality), and the cross-reference to `kroneckers-jugendtraum`.

references.title: Theorie der abel'schen Zahlkörper
references.author: Heinrich Weber
references.venue: Acta Mathematica, vol. 8, pp. 193–263; vol. 9, pp. 105–130
references.description: Weber's completion of the Kronecker–Weber theorem (Kronecker 1853 announced, Hilbert 1896 patched a gap): every finite abelian extension of ℚ is contained in some cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n)$. The proof systematically uses **conductor theory** — the minimal $N$ such that $K \subseteq \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_N)$ — which is exactly the missing Mathlib ingredient identified in keyInsight #2 and keyInsight #6 (~500 Lean lines of conductor theory to close the abelian case of Shafarevich). Weber's paper introduced the modern conductor formalism that the file's `galois_compositum_product` axiom would invoke once formalized: coprime conductors → coprime discriminants → linear disjointness → product Galois group on compositum.

references.title: Gleichungen mit vorgeschriebener Gruppe
references.author: Emmy Noether
references.description: Noether's program for the **inverse Galois problem via rationality of fixed fields**: given a finite group $G$ acting faithfully on $\mathbb{Q}(x_1, \ldots, x_n)$ by permuting variables, when is the fixed field $\mathbb{Q}(x_1, \ldots, x_n)^G$ purely transcendental over $\mathbb{Q}$? If it is, **Hilbert's irreducibility theorem** specializes generic parameters to realize $G$ as a Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$. Swan (1969) gave the first counterexample ($G = \mathbb{Z}/47$, despite cyclic groups being trivially Shafarevich-realizable — Noether's *method* fails even when realizability holds). Lenstra (1974) extended this to all $\mathbb{Z}/p^n$ for $n \geq 3$ at certain primes. The historical lesson, central to this file's status-report framing: **realization and constructive realization are different problems**. Shafarevich (1954) settles realization for solvable groups, but constructive Noetherian realization remains open for most groups. Cited in the historicalContext.

references.title: Beweis eines Hauptsatzes in der Theorie der Algebren
references.author: Adrian Albert, Richard Brauer, Helmut Hasse, Emmy Noether
references.venue: Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik, vol. 167, pp. 399–404 (Brauer–Hasse–Noether portion); see also Albert (1931) for independent discovery
references.description: The **Albert–Brauer–Hasse–Noether theorem**: a central simple algebra over a number field $K$ is split by $K$ iff it is split at every completion $K_v$ — the local-global principle for the Brauer group, giving the exact sequence $0 \to \text{Br}(K) \to \bigoplus_v \text{Br}(K_v) \to \mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z} \to 0$. This is the **engine of Shafarevich's solution to the non-abelian embedding problems**: discharging the $H^2$ obstruction to lifting a $G/N$-extension to a $G$-extension reduces, via Hochschild–Serre and the Brauer-group identification, to verifying local solvability everywhere — which is automatic when the obstruction class vanishes locally. Cited in openQuestion #2 as the foundational gap for non-abelian solvable Shafarevich in Mathlib. The 2013 IHÉS workshop and Roquette's 2005 monograph trace the simultaneous-discovery history.

references.title: Duality theorems in Galois cohomology over number fields
references.author: John Tate
references.venue: Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians (Stockholm), Mittag-Leffler, pp. 288–295
references.description: Tate's 1962 ICM announcement of the **Tate–Poitou duality theorem**: for a finite Galois module $M$ over a number field $K$, the global cohomology groups $H^i(K, M)$ fit into a nine-term exact sequence relating $H^i$, $H^{2-i}$ of the dual module, and local cohomology at all completions — the **culmination of the local-global framework for Galois cohomology**. Poitou independently developed the duality in 1967. Tate–Poitou is the deepest classical tool gating Shafarevich's solution of non-abelian solvable embedding problems: each embedding problem reduces to a $H^2$ obstruction, and Tate–Poitou provides the exact sequence that lets one discharge the obstruction by computing $H^1$ on the dual side. Cited in openQuestion #3 as a **foundational gap in Mathlib's number theory** — full Shafarevich requires Tate–Poitou, which itself is a multi-year formalization project.

references.title: Cohomology of group extensions
references.author: Gerhard Hochschild, Jean-Pierre Serre
references.venue: Transactions of the American Mathematical Society, vol. 74, no. 1, pp. 110–134
references.description: The **Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence**: for a normal subgroup $N \triangleleft G$ with quotient $Q = G/N$ and a $G$-module $M$, there is a spectral sequence $E_2^{p,q} = H^p(Q, H^q(N, M)) \Rightarrow H^{p+q}(G, M)$ that organizes the cohomology of $G$ in terms of the cohomology of $N$ and $Q$. **The structural backbone of Shafarevich's embedding-problem strategy**: induct on a composition series $\{e\} = N_0 \triangleleft N_1 \triangleleft \cdots \triangleleft N_k = G$ with abelian quotients, lifting Galois extensions one composition factor at a time, using the spectral sequence to control obstructions to each lifting step. Cited in keyInsight #2 and openQuestion #2 as essential machinery for non-abelian solvable Shafarevich, currently absent from Mathlib. The 1953 paper is the foundational reference, with modern textbook treatments in Neukirch-Schmidt-Wingberg (Reference 5) and Serre's *Galois Cohomology* (Reference 6).

references.title: Abhyankar's conjecture on Galois groups over curves
references.author: David Harbater
references.description: Harbater's **patching theorem** for Galois extensions of function fields in positive characteristic, jointly with Raynaud's parallel proof (1994), settles Abhyankar's conjecture: a finite group $G$ is the Galois group of an unramified cover of $\mathbb{A}^1_{\overline{\mathbb{F}_p}}$ iff $G$ is generated by its quasi-$p$ subgroups (i.e., subgroups whose order has no factor coprime to $p$). The patching technique — gluing local Galois covers via formal-geometric rigidity — gave a function-field analog of Shafarevich's number-field theorem and was extended by Harbater–Pop–Stevenson and later by Haran–Jarden to the *full inverse Galois problem over $\overline{\mathbb{F}_p}(t)$*. Cited in openQuestion #4 as the natural function-field generalization of the inverse Galois problem this file would extend to. Mathlib has no analytic-geometric machinery for patching, making this a long-term goal.
